correctness.rationale: Rotational orthogonality gives squared monomial norm π² μ(n), μ(n)=∫_0¹ s^n exp[-2(log(e/(1-s)))^α]ds; axis kernel K=π^-2 Σ r^(2n)/μ(n). Setting x=-log(r²), a(t)=-log μ(t), differentiation of log Z(x)=log Σ exp[a(n)-xn] verifies exact β²=Var_x(N)/r² (no lost π or factor two). For the continuous μ(t), q=1-s gives strictly concave H_t(q)=t log(1-q)-2log(e/q)^α; mode q_t solves tq/(1-q)=B_t=2α(log(e/q))^(α-1), q_t~B_t/t, B_t~2α(log t)^(α-1)→∞ since α>1. Gaussian Laplace curvature and controlled tails imply a’(t)~B_t/t and -a’’(t)~B_t/t², not merely pointwise local quadratic fit. Unique discrete saddle a’(t_x)=x gives t_x~2α x^-1(log 1/x)^(α-1), variance asymptotically 1/(-a’’(t_x))~2α x^-2(log 1/x)^(α-1) from discrete local CLT/tangent-tail concentration. Therefore β coefficient sqrt(2α); radial induced metric and dL/dr~2/(1-r²) give axis-distance coefficient sqrt(2α)/(α+1). Independent numerical quadrature of actual moments for α=1.5,2.0 and δ=.05,.02,.01 found finite variance/predicted ratios decreasing from ~1.39 to ~1.36 and ~1.30 to ~1.26 with negligible n-tail masses; slow convergence is not a proof. Direct differentiation of moment series and both saddle curvatures checked. The endpoint α=1 has a different exact Bergman coefficient, as correctly excluded; ambient geodesic distance is not identified.
